entities.name: Saikosaponin B2
observations: Naturally occurring plant terpenoid from Bupleurum species, including Bupleurum kaoi/root; saikosaponins are oleanane-type pentacyclic triterpenoid glycosides.
The primary HCV study explicitly describes saikosaponin B2 as a naturally occurring terpenoid.

entities.name: PMID:25450204
observations: Lin et al., Journal of Hepatology (2015), evaluated saikosaponin B2 in infectious HCV culture systems across genotypes/clinical isolates and in primary human hepatocytes.

Entry was directly assessed: particle neutralization, reduced attachment, inhibition of entry/fusion, interaction with HCV E2, reduced serum-derived HCV binding to hepatoma cells, and prevention of primary-hepatocyte infection.

The study reported potent inhibition at non-cytotoxic concentrations and localized the major effect to early entry; replication/translation, egress, and spread were relatively unaffected in the reported life-cycle analyses.
The retrieved abstract did not provide a numerical entry IC50, EC50, tested concentration, or percent inhibition.

entities.name: PMID:30920421
observations: A 2019 cell-culture-derived HCV study reported that saikosaponin B2 inhibited viral entry, replication, and translation, but the retrieved abstract lacked detailed entry-assay information and numerical potency.
